entities.summary: Aryabhata (b. 476 CE, Pataliputra, Magadha, in the Gupta Empire; d. 550 CE) stands as a monumental figure in the Classical era, a polymath whose groundbreaking work in mathematics and astronomy profoundly shaped not only Indian intellectual traditions but also global scientific thought. His treatise, the *Aryabhatiya*, written around 499 CE, codified a sophisticated understanding of numerical systems, celestial mechanics, and trigonometry, establishing him as a pioneer whose insights would ripple across continents and centuries. Operating from the intellectual hub of Pataliputra, Aryabhata's contributions were foundational, marking a high point in ancient Indian science.

historicalSignificance.significanceNarrative: Aryabhata's introduction of the place-value system with zero as a placeholder, accurate calculation of pi, and innovative astronomical models profoundly influenced subsequent Indian and Islamic scientific thought. His work laid critical groundwork for the development of algebra and trigonometry, impacting global mathematics for centuries.
